subject: LumenAI pilot — TTFT expectations and streaming payload pacing
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumenai.com>, eng-ops@lumenai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: LumenAI pilot — TTFT expectations and streaming payload pacing

Thanks again for the call earlier, Aisha — quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same frame.

Summary of the ask (as I heard it):
- Web client: sub-200ms perceived startup (TTFT) target for typical single-turn summaries (average payload ~350 tokens).
- Expected sustained load: ~400–600 RPS aggregate across regions to start, with burst tolerance to ~900 RPS for short windows.
- Browser clients prefer SSE for simplicity; mobile apps may use WebSocket.
- Concern: client-side rendering shows blank UI for ~300–500ms today; they want visible partial streaming.

Proposed Redwood targets / pilot scope:
- TTFT target: p95 <= 120–160ms on dedicated pilot nodes (we can relax to 200ms for first week of pilot).
- Streaming: prefer SSE for the web pilot (easier with existing infra). Recommend chunk cadence 80–120ms for the first-party UI to keep perceived interactivity.
- Concurrency/throughput: start pilot at 50–100 concurrent connections per instance, scale to ~500 concurrent across the pool. Aim for 500 RPS sustained.
- Fallback policy: if TTFT exceeds 300ms or chunking drops below 1 chunk/sec for >5s, fall back to a lower-cost model variant to preserve response flow.

Data / instrumentation we need from LumenAI to size the pilot:
1) typical request size distribution (input token counts) — a histogram is ideal.
2) outbound payload sizes (average generated tokens per response).
3) Synchronous vs streaming client preference split (web vs mobile).

Attachments: I attached a short SLO proposal (slo-proposal-lumenai.pdf) and a request for network traces if you can share.

Next steps / timeline:
- Aisha: share the sample network traces and anonymized token distribution (if available) by EOD Monday.
- Redwood: build a 2-week pilot plan and runbook once we have traces (Marissa & Karthik to draft).
- Kickoff: propose Tue 9/22 for a 1-hour pilot kickoff demo + perf baseline.

Thanks — happy to adjust targets if any of the assumptions above are off.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0118

(attachments: slo-proposal-lumenai.pdf)

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side and attaching the network traces you requested.

Clarifications / constraints from LumenAI:
- Target: we'd like to shoot for p95 <= 200ms on web for launch; if you can show 120–160ms in pilot that's ideal and we can push for faster in prod.
- Traffic profile: our initial region is US-east, expected 500 RPS baseline coming out of our edge (we can throttle).
- Client-side: web will use SSE; mobile teams would prefer a single WS path (they're on a slightly older SDK).
- Feature: we need partial tokens to render streamed bullets as they arrive — chunk sizes should be small but not noisy.

Attached: lumenai-network-traces.zip contains a 15-min sample from our staging environment and a CSV with request size distribution.

Question: for SSE chunk cadence, what's the recommended tradeoff between perceived interactivity and token-overhead? Also, what measurement will Redwood provide during the pilot (we need the per-request TTFT, chunk latency, and dropped-chunk counts).

We'll be available for the kickoff Tue 9/22 morning PT — prefer 9:00–11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Product, LumenAI
aisha.khan@lumenai.com

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding the customer's confirmation and traces. Key asks: p95 TTFT target between 120–200ms depending on what we demonstrate; SSE preferred for web; chunk cadence ~80–120ms ideal.

My suggestion for the pilot config (initial):
- Dedicated pilot pool: 4 instances (A100 equivalent) behind our smart router, region us-east.
- Model: opt-7b-cuda-quant (or equivalent fast-decoder variant) to minimize kernel overhead.
- Batching: small continuous batching with a 5ms micro-batch window to keep TTFT low.
- Chunking: server-driven chunking, target ~60–120ms cadence; envelope partial tokens every 60–80ms for low-latency clients.
- Metrics to collect: TTFT (p50/p95/p99), per-chunk latency, chunks-per-response, tail-latency heatmaps, CPU/GPU utilization, and any KV cache hit/miss stats.

Pilot run plan:
1) Baseline (no caching) — 1 hour of synthetic steady 200 RPS, measure TTFT curve.
2) Realistic traffic replay using customer's traces — 2 hours with traffic shaping to 500 RPS.
3) Stress bursts — 5-minute bursts to 900 RPS to observe graceful degradation and fallback behavior.

Assumptions: we can get the traces and a shared measurement mapping from LumenAI by Monday; the customer is OK with a short maintenance window during burst tests.

Action items:
- Marissa: draft the pilot runbook and SLO doc (attach baseline thresholds).
- Karthik: can you validate the model/instance choices and prepare a quick perf script? Focus on micro-batching params + SSE vs WS differences.

I'll schedule the kickoff for Tue 9/22 09:30 PT unless Aisha confirms a different time.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: LumenAI pilot — TTFT expectations and streaming payload pacing

Thanks all — reviewed the traces quickly, and a couple of notes after a quick pass:

Observations from traces (high level):
- Median request size ~280 tokens, 95th ~920 tokens (so chunk counts will vary).
- Most responses are 150–450 generated tokens.
- Client RTTs in the staging traces average 35–75ms — good news for hitting lower TTFT on dedicated infra.

Pilot runbook & SLO proposal:
- Draft uploaded (pilot-runbook-v1.md) — it includes the three-phase run plan Rishi outlined, explicit measurement points, and a rollback/fallback checklist.
- Initial SLOs for the pilot: TTFT p95 <= 160ms (goal 120ms). Streaming cadence: median chunk interval 90ms, 90% of responses > 2 chunks.
- Ramp plan: start at 200 RPS synthetic, then replay at 500 RPS. We'll capture per-request traces to correlate chunk count to perceived UI staleness.

Karthik: can you prioritize the perf script that toggles micro-batch windows (3ms / 5ms / 10ms) and chunk cadence (60ms / 90ms / 150ms)? Also add a mode to test SSE vs WS differences (payload and handshake overhead).

Aisha: please confirm the kickoff time (Rishi suggested 9:30 PT Tue) and share any internal stakeholders who should attend (product, mobile eng, infra). If you can grant a short-lived access token for traffic replay to our staging harness that will speed things up (we'll delete it after the test).

I'll attach the runbook now.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
